sources.citation: Otero, Manuel A. 2019. A Historical Reconstruction of the Koman Language Family. PhD dissertation, University of Oregon.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; 'stress' and 'accent' occur zero times in the dissertation. Sec. 2.1.7 (pp. 76-85) gives Opo consonants, vowels, ATR harmony and tone: 'one defining feature of the Opo cluster is the presence of four contrastive level tones' (L, M, H, XH) plus grammatical tone in verb stems; fn. 61 summarises Bender 1983 ('distinctive tone is probable'), Lemi 2010 ('at least low and high tones'), van Silfhout 2013:36 ('at least a high and a low tone'), Mellese 2017 (three levels).

sources.citation: Smolders, Joshua A. G. 2019. Nominal and verbal number in Bilugu Opo. Studies in African Linguistics 48(1): 133-184. doi:10.32473/sal.v48i1.114929
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 1.5 Phonological overview (pp. 138-140): 32 consonants, seven vowels /2IU/, contrastive vowel length, and 'Tone in Opo has a high lexical and grammatical functional load.. four levels of phonemic tone in Bilugu: low (L), mid (M), high (H), and extra-high (X)'.

sources.citation: Mellese Gelaneh Alemu. 2017 [title page dated 2016]. Documentation and Grammatical Description of Tapo. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. xiv+236 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 3 Phonology (pp. 16-49) covers consonants, vowels, ATR harmony, syllable structure, tone (3.4, pp. 44-45: 'Tapo is a tonal language with three contrasting tones' H/M/L, TBU = vowel, grammatical tone on verb-final vowels) and morphophonemics; the words stress/accent do not occur anywhere in the (Acrobat-scanned) text.
